_source: AI-researched venue CANDIDATES for Manchester and Cheshire, awaiting review — never directly edited by the research agent. Populated by a daily scheduled research agent (2026-08, at explicit user request: 'fan out some research agents who's goal is to run every day to find and suggest new businesses... they shouldn't go beyond cheshire and manchester just yet'; bumped from ~3-5/day to 10/day at a later explicit request). See .claude/agents/curia-research-daily.md for the full research brief/rules this agent works under (Hard rule 1 chain/fast-food screening, real coordinates only, no duplicates, Do/Drink/Eat coverage balance). The research agent commits straight to master for this file (no PR — this queue has zero effect on the live app, nothing reads it except the review agent and the admin dashboard's Growth Insights context). A second, independent daily agent (.claude/agents/curia-suggestion-review.md) re-verifies each `pending` entry and is the thing that promotes one into the real docs/data/venues.json, pushing straight to master after its own independent re-verification (see that file's own 2026-09-04 doc comment for why the human checkpoint moved to Curia Command's Pending Review tab instead of a PR here). Each entry mirrors docs/data/venues.json's own raw shape (name/district/type/spend/lat/lon/base/bands/reason) exactly, so a reviewed-and-approved entry can be moved into that file with a straight copy-paste, plus review-only fields (suggestedDate, status, researchNotes) that get stripped on promotion. `district` values must be a real existing district id from docs/data/districts.json (manchester/cheshire metros only) UNLESS the entry is itself proposing a brand-new district — see district-suggestions.json for that case instead; a venue suggestion should never invent a district id that doesn't exist anywhere.
_reviewWorkflow: status starts 'pending' on every new entry. The daily curia-suggestion-review agent changes it to 'approved'/promoted (then copies the venue fields into docs/data/venues.json and removes the entry here, pushed straight to master) or 'rejected' (left here with researchNotes explaining why, as a record so the same candidate isn't re-suggested later — curia-research-daily checks every entry here regardless of status before suggesting anything new). Genuinely uncertain candidates go to docs/data/pending-review-queue.json instead, staying 'pending' here until a human decides via Curia Command. A human's actual review happens by reading Curia Command's daily briefing and Pending Review tab, not by editing this file directly, though a human reviewer (or a future admin-dashboard screen) can still hand-edit an entry's status here if needed.

suggestions.name: Clark Art
suggestions.reason: Bill Clark's own gallery on Ashley Road since 1999, deep in L.S. Lowry and the northern painters he's written the books on — a private dealer's eye, not a gallery chain's algorithm.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Clark Art (155 Ashley Road, Hale) closed permanently on 3 October 2024 after 18 years, per Bill Clark's own retirement announcement (reported by Altrincham Today, 'An incredible journey: Clark Art to close after 18 years in Hale village'). The prior research pass's sources (Tripadvisor/Artsy/halebarns.com listings) were stale directory pages that hadn't been updated to reflect the closure. Do not re-suggest — the gallery no longer exists.

suggestions.name: Yang Sing
suggestions.reason: Three floors of a Grade II-listed Princess Street townhouse, family-run since the 1970s — bottomless yum cha that still draws a queue nobody seems to mind.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Yang Sing (34 Princess Street) has been closed since December 2021/early 2022 (kitchen fire, then a lease dispute) and Yang Sing Limited is now in liquidation per Companies House — it never reopened despite the owner's 2022 hope to reopen by 2023/24. The prior research pass's sources (visitmanchester.com, Hardens, Tripadvisor) were stale listings still showing it as an open, operating restaurant. Do not re-suggest unless it demonstrably reopens under new ownership.

suggestions.name: Blue Lobster
suggestions.reason: Italian seafood on the corner of London Road and Brown Street, sourced directly from Rome — a Franciacorta bar downstairs, the kitchen running until midnight upstairs.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Blue Lobster (34 London Road, Alderley Edge) closed permanently in December 2017, less than nine months after its April 2017 opening, following a staff-payment dispute with owner Andrea Zecchino (reported by alderleyedge.com and Manchester Confidential at the time). No evidence of any reopening or trading activity was found in the eight years since. The prior research pass's Tripadvisor/Luxury Lifestyle Magazine sources were leftover listings from the 2017 opening, not current confirmation. Do not re-suggest unless it demonstrably reopens under new ownership.

suggestions.name: Fire Station Social Cucina
suggestions.reason: A pizza theatre and wood oven where Gusto used to sit on London Road — hand-rolled pasta, Napoli-style bases, and only one other room anywhere doing the same thing.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via thebusinessdesk.com, wilmslow.co.uk/alderleyedge.com and the operator's own site (firestationsocial.co.uk): Fire Station Social Cucina, 75 London Road, Alderley Edge SK9 7DY, opened 10 June 2026 in the former Gusto unit — the second site for this specific concept, after the original in Tarporley. Run by 'Project Social Cucina', the restaurant division of Cheshire Pub Company (a separate entity from the 7-pub Cheshire Cat group already referenced elsewhere in this file) — only 2 sites confirmed under the Fire Station Social Cucina name itself, the same 2-site sibling precedent already used for Cibo/Suburban Green/Smoke Wilmslow/Heddy's/Caramello. Flagged for the reviewer: the parent company's own press describes this as 'expansion', so worth a quick re-check at promotion time that a third site hasn't since appeared. Moderate-high confidence otherwise — real, recently opened, well-covered locally, no closure signals. Re-checked again 2026-09-08 (curia-suggestion-review daily pass) specifically for a rumoured third site: none found — same 2-site status as this note originally recorded, still pending, still in docs/data/pending-review-queue.json for a human call rather than re-decided here. DECIDED 2026-09-08 by direct user instruction, in an interactive session: promoted into venues.json with the new `status: 'coming-soon'` field (added the same day specifically for this case) rather than a flat yes/no — real venue, passes Hard rule 1 on site count today, but its editorial confidence marker stays provisional given the parent's stated expansion plans. See venues.json's own note on the new field.

suggestions.name: The Copper Room
suggestions.reason: Amy and Rick Armstrong crowdfunded their way into Charles Roe House's Grade II* rooms — steak and seafood cooked properly, in a silk merchant's own dining room on Chestergate.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via the operator's own site (chefrick.co.uk), Macclesfield Nub News (two separate pieces confirming both the Kickstarter-funded opening and the venue name) and Tripadvisor (active listing with 2026-dated reviews): The Copper Room, Charles Roe House, 60-62 Chestergate, Macclesfield SK11 6DY, a fine-dining restaurant and cocktail bar run by chef-owners Amy and Rick Armstrong. No second site or group ownership found anywhere — single-site, independently owned, passes Hard rule 1 cleanly. Coordinates from doogal.co.uk's postcode geocode for SK11 6DY. Reuses the existing FINE DINING type. Fills a real gap: Macclesfield had only 1 Eat-category venue (Chestergate Bistro) against 2 Do and 3 Drink before this addition. REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-14: the chef-owned fine-dining concept this candidate described no longer trades at 60-62 Chestergate. Charles Roe House's dining room changed to 'Piccante at The Copper Room' (Italian/Brazilian tapas, opened Dec 2022) and per Macclesfield Nub News that room has sat empty since summer 2025 while the building is converted into a different, unrelated venture, 'The Charles Roe Pub' (reopening Dec 2025). Amy and Rick Armstrong's ownership story checks out, but whatever they run today is not trading at this address under this description — a closure/identity mismatch, not a chain issue. Do not re-suggest at this address; a genuinely reopened Armstrong-run venue elsewhere would need its own fresh verification.

suggestions.name: Prana
suggestions.reason: Two floors of proper acoustics on Ashley Road from the team behind Stockport's Amp — order the cocktail, but the stage is the reason to stay past nine.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-22: Google Maps marks it 'Permanently closed' (posting disabled), its own site returns a dead Cloudflare error, Instagram/Facebook are gone, Skiddle shows zero events ever listed, and its sister venue (Amp, Stockport) also closed and reopened under an unrelated name/concept. The property itself (14-16 Ashley Road) is listed for sale as former restaurant premises. Companies House shows an 'Active' shell (PRANA F&B LIMITED) with overdue first accounts — not evidence of an operating business. Do not re-suggest.

suggestions.name: Mouro Coffee Bar
suggestions.reason: Moroccan tile underfoot and a La Marzocco machine doing the actual work — focaccia sandwiches, matcha and affogato for a stretch of Heaton Moor Road that doesn't need to shout about any of it.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via Tripadvisor (5.0/5, current 2026 listing), the Food Standards Agency ratings register and the venue's own Instagram (@mourocoffeebar): Mouro Coffee Bar, 72 Heaton Moor Road, Stockport SK4 4NZ — a design-led independent coffee bar serving speciality coffee, cold-pressed juices, pastries and focaccia sandwiches. No second site or group ownership found anywhere despite a direct search; single-site, passes Hard rule 1 cleanly. Coordinates from postcode geocode for SK4 4NZ. Reuses the existing BRUNCH SPOT type. Heaton Moor was at 8 venues (3 Do, 3 Drink, 2 Eat) before this addition — Eat was its thinnest category, and the district is one of ten currently under the 10-venue standing target. High confidence. REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-16: the 'no second site found anywhere' claim doesn't hold up — Mouro is in fact a real, actively expanding four-site coffee brand: the original Heaton Moor site, two Altrincham sites (25 Market Street and 8-10 Oxford Road, opened August 2025), and a fourth opened 16 May 2026 on Tib Street in the Northern Quarter itself (themanc.com's own coverage explicitly headlines it 'Mouro opens third coffee shop', undercounting even by its own count since two Altrincham sites exist). This is well past this file's established 2-3-site small-sibling-group allowance and spans two separate towns plus a city-centre expansion — a real, currently-growing chain by Hard rule 1's own standard, not a family pair. Do not re-suggest unless the brand's footprint materially contracts.

suggestions.name: Underbank
suggestions.reason: A former bank branch turned beer hall and soundsystem room at the crossroads of the two Underbanks — Pomona Island and Runaway on tap, and a rig loud enough that conversation moves to the beer garden after ten.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-22: investigated as a suspected name/identity mismatch with the existing 'The Underbank' catalog entry (same building, 27 Great Underbank). Found no evidence a second real venue exists — the theory traced to a January 2025 Instagram announcement (Benji Taylor's own plan for a live-music venue in the same building) that appears to have been superseded by what actually opened in May 2025 (the O'Malleys' 'The Underbank', which itself runs gigs/comedy/quiz nights, not just a beer hall). The existing catalog entry's name and core facts are correct as-is. Do not re-suggest as a separate venue without direct on-the-ground confirmation.

suggestions.name: Olive Tree Brasserie
suggestions.reason: Meze and a bottomless brunch on Watergate Row since 2016 — Dean Wilson's third room, not his first draft, and it still runs on a Greek kitchen's own instincts.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-22: the original candidate's '3rd site, Lytham/Preston/Chester' framing understated the real scale — the group's own site today lists FOUR active locations (Chester, Leeds, Lytham, Stockton Heath) across three counties, plus a closed 5th site (Preston, liquidated 2021). Founder/director Dean Wilson was disqualified from running any company for 10.5 years in Nov 2024 after fraudulently claiming ~£200k in COVID Bounce Back Loans across the group's per-site companies. A genuine multi-city regional chain, not a small group — do not re-suggest.

suggestions.name: Bali Health Lounge
suggestions.reason: Three floors above George Street built around ELEMIS facials and a tea lounge — Chinatown's actual quiet room, one flight up from everything loud below it.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-22, overturning an earlier 'moderate-high confidence, still trading' read: the operating company (Bali Health Lounge Limited, #07411581, same address) passed a creditors' voluntary liquidation resolution in Dec 2022 and was formally dissolved 4 Dec 2024 (The Gazette, Companies House). The 'live' Yelp/Tripadvisor activity that misled the earlier pass is uncurated listing pages carrying stale marketing copy with auto-generated 'Updated' headers regardless of actual status — no genuinely-dated 2023-2026 review or evidence of a relaunch was found. Do not re-suggest unless a new operator/relaunch is confirmed.

suggestions.name: The Nest Nantwich
suggestions.reason: Nick Wadeson's own copper still, Valerie, still runs on Pepper Street — the family behind Three Wrens Gin poured their production room into a proper cocktail bar rather than settling for a tasting counter.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED — exact duplicate of a venue already live in docs/data/venues.json under the identical name and coordinates (a different real venue on Pepper Street, Nantwich, already catalogued as a cocktail bar with its own working still). The pipeline's dedup logic only checks this suggestions file, not venues.json itself, so it missed the collision. Do not re-suggest.

suggestions.name: Amici
suggestions.reason: Italian-Greek tapas in the Village Square, run by Andrea, Giovanni and Chris on a menu that never quite picks a country — steak and seafood mains for whoever wants to stop sharing.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED — exact duplicate of a venue already live in docs/data/venues.json under the identical name, district and coordinates (Bramhall, Italian-Greek tapas, Andrea/Giovanni/Chris). Same dedup gap as The Nest Nantwich/Amazing India in this same batch. Do not re-suggest.

suggestions.name: Amazing India
suggestions.reason: Joby Joy's South Indian room on Pickford Street, the only one of its kind in town — dosas and a party hall that means the celebration doesn't have to end when the curry does.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED — exact duplicate of a venue already live in docs/data/venues.json under the identical name, district and near-identical coordinates (Macclesfield, South Indian, Pickford Street). Same dedup gap as The Nest Nantwich/Amici in this same batch. Do not re-suggest.

suggestions.name: King Street Kitchen
suggestions.reason: Small, family-run, and on King Street since long before the brunch queue started forming outside it — a plant-based option on every course, not just the one everyone else bothers with.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED — this venue was already investigated, confirmed closed (two independent listing sites marking it CLOSED, corroborated by a local Facebook post) and removed from docs/data/venues.json on 2026-09-08 (see docs/data/pending-review-queue.json's own record of that decision). The daily research pipeline re-suggested it again on 2026-09-22 without checking that history — a real dedup gap (this file's own dedup logic only checks entries within this file, not venues.json's removal/closure history). Do not re-suggest; if the pipeline's dedup logic gets fixed, this is the case that should have caught it.

suggestions.name: Coco Tang
suggestions.reason: Eighteen years of running Nottingham's Byard Lane before Manchester got a look — Vietnamese café by day, a cocktail room and late kitchen once the Bridge Street lights come on.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via restaurantonline.co.uk and premierconstructionnews.com's own coverage of the Manchester opening, plus Tripadvisor/Instagram for the original Nottingham site: Coco Tang, taking over the former SakkuSamba/Artisan unit at 1 The Avenue, Bridge Street, Spinningfields, opening autumn 2026 — an independent Vietnamese café, restaurant, private dining space and late-night cocktail bar/club, run by the same owners as the 18-year-old original Coco Tang in Nottingham (Byard Lane). A real 2-site pair across two cities, industry press explicitly describing it as 'independent' rather than a chain expansion — within the same 'single sibling in another city' precedent already established in this file (e.g. Craig's, Ivy Spinningfields). No third site found. District placement: industry coverage explicitly calls the address 'Spinningfields'/'Bridge Street in Spinningfields' despite 1 The Avenue sitting right at the Deansgate boundary; coordinates approximated from the John Rylands Library/1 The Avenue building's known location (postcode-geocoding blocked this session) since the exact unit number wasn't published at time of writing — flagged for the reviewer to tighten once the venue is trading and a precise address is published. Reuses the existing VIETNAMESE type. Spinningfields' real Eat category (Celebratory, Fine Dining, Small Plates) was its thinnest before this addition. Moderate-high confidence — the venue and ownership are well-documented; the exact coordinate and the opening date (announced, not yet independently confirmed as trading) are the flagged caveats.

suggestions.name: Thom's Bar & Kitchen
suggestions.reason: Thom Collins runs the wine and cocktail list, his parents run the room — a family concern on Heaton Moor Road that's never needed a rebrand to stay full.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED 2026-10-09 (curia-suggestion-review, independent re-verification): 54 Heaton Moor Road no longer trades as Thom's. CAMRA's own record for this address shows Thom's Wine Bar became Scarlet Door (late 2022), which closed 7 Sept 2024, and the site reopened 18 Nov 2024 under a new name, 'Eden' — which is already a live venue in the database under heaton-moor. This candidate is a stale identity for an address that's already catalogued under its current name; don't re-suggest Thom's at 54 Heaton Moor Road.

suggestions.name: Little Tap
suggestions.reason: A former butcher's shop turned craft beer and cocktail den on Tarporley's high street — Myles Carr split the kitchen off across the road once the bar itself got too busy to also cook.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED 2026-10-09 (curia-suggestion-review, independent re-verification): Confirmed permanently closed. The Morning Advertiser (24 June 2026, 'Independent Cheshire bar closes with immediate effect') reports Little Tap & Terrarium, Tarporley, closed immediately on 22 June 2026, owner citing rising costs and cost pressure on independent hospitality; CAMRA's listing for both Little Tap and its sibling Terrarium by Little Tap mark them 'Closed Long Term' from the same date. This closure happened three months before this suggestion's 2026-09-23 date, so the original researchNotes' 'high confidence, no closure signals' finding was simply wrong/stale. Note the sibling venue 'Terrarium by Little Tap' is also separately pending in the queue (tarporley) and should be rejected for the same reason.

suggestions.name: Saul Hay Gallery
suggestions.reason: A railway cottage behind the old Bass Warehouse, hung with contemporary painting and sculpture nobody's pitching as an investment — Castlefield's actual private-dealer gallery.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED 2026-10-09 (curia-suggestion-review, independent re-verification): The gallery is closing its physical Castlefield premises. Manchester Wire and Art Rabbit/Creative Tourist confirm Saul Hay Gallery ran its landmark final exhibition, '10x10' (100 artists, marking 10 years), 13–28 June 2026, after which it vacates Railway Cottage, Castle Street and moves to a mobile/online model with occasional temporary-space shows rather than a fixed walk-in gallery. As of today (2026-10-09) there is no longer a standing gallery at this address to recommend. Also flag for whoever re-researches: the address itself (Castle Street, behind the old Bass Warehouse) is Castlefield, not really Deansgate proper — fine under this app's districts since there's no separate Castlefield district id, but worth knowing if a different, still-operating Castlefield gallery is suggested later.

suggestions.name: By AdiVa
suggestions.reason: Adi Joseph's own edit of European labels and considered gifts on Ashley Road, enough of a fixture on the village high street that regulars have long since dropped the 'By'.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via Instagram (@by_adiva, current posted hours), Facebook and business directory listings (clothes-shops.co.uk, hale-eng.business-dir.co.uk): By AdiVa, 192 Ashley Road, Hale, Altrincham WA15 9SF — an independent women's fashion and luxury gift boutique run by Adi Joseph, described in local coverage as a long-standing fixture of Hale village high street. A related 'Adiva Interiors' Facebook page exists under what appears to be the same owner/brand, but no second fashion-boutique site was found; single-site, passes Hard rule 1 cleanly. Coordinates from the WA15 9SF postcode centroid (web geocode search) — WA15 is Hale's own postcode district (WA14 covers Altrincham/Bowdon), and 192 Ashley Road sits closer to Hale's district centroid than Altrincham's. Reuses the existing FASHION BOUTIQUE type (Beaumont Organic, Northern Quarter; Tuula, Alderley Edge). Closes a real gap: Hale's Do category (Contemporary Six Hale, Hale Country Club & Spa, InHale Yoga, Hale Lawn Tennis Club) had no Clothes-shopping-tile venue despite Hale's own high street being widely and specifically documented for exactly this. Moderate-high confidence — well-documented, current social activity, no closure signals.

suggestions.name: No.8 Dukes
suggestions.reason: Duke's Court stays lit long after the rest of Macclesfield has gone home — doors open to 3am, seven nights, in a room that doesn't bother pretending it's anything but the town's last stop.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via creativetourist.com, Companies House (NO.8 DUKES LIMITED, company 13034680), macclesfield.nub.news (multiple articles on owner Kyle Frost-Morgan/Dukes Hospitality Group), pubsgalore.co.uk and restaurantguru.com: No.8 Dukes, 8 Dukes Court, Mill Street, Macclesfield SK11 6NN — a plush, exposed-brick cocktail bar open 10pm-3am seven nights, Macclesfield's self-described 'exclusive late night venue'. Ownership: Kyle Frost-Morgan's Dukes Hospitality Group, which also runs Dukebox, The White Lion, Duchess and The Ivy Leaf (bars) plus Duke's Deli, Total Aesthetics and Total Tanning — a genuine 5-bar local footprint, but every single one sits in or around Duke's Court, Macclesfield town centre; no venue found anywhere outside the town. Flagged explicitly for the review agent: this is a bigger local footprint than a single sibling, but reads as one operator building out one small town's nightlife (the same shape as The Salt House Ltd's 3 Northwich sites, see Bull Ring NW above), not a multi-city chain. Coordinates from the SK11 6NN postcode centroid (doogal.co.uk/checkmypostcode, 53.257233/-2.125601). Reuses the existing COCKTAIL BAR type. Closes Macclesfield's real late-night Drink gap — its one existing Drink venue in this register (Diversion Bar & Kitchen) is typed LATE-NIGHT LOUNGE, not COCKTAIL BAR. Moderate confidence given the ownership footprint noted above — genuinely current and well-documented, no closure signals.

suggestions.name: Ek's Kitchen
suggestions.reason: Twenty covers on School Lane and a chef with thirty years behind the wok — order the specials a day ahead, or take your chances in the queue with everyone else.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via Tripadvisor (active 2026 listing and reviews), Wanderlog, the venue's own site (ekskitchen.co.uk, copyright 2026) and its own social presence: Ek's Kitchen, 177 School Lane, Didsbury, Manchester M19 1GN — a small (roughly 20-cover), family-run, halal Thai restaurant, Chef Ek credited with 30 years' experience, reservations and 1-day-ahead pre-orders recommended given limited seating. Flagged for the review agent: the M19 1GN postcode geocodes to 53.415407/-2.217513, about 1km south-east of the Didsbury district centroid (53.4176/-2.2310) and technically nearer Ladybarn/Burnage than Didsbury Village or West Didsbury's Burton Road — however the venue's own branding, social handles and every independent listing found consistently self-identify it as 'Didsbury', and the coordinate still sits closer to Didsbury than to any other Curia district, so it's suggested under didsbury rather than left out; genuinely worth a second look given the postcode's own ward. No other locations of this specific restaurant found anywhere in searches — a single, small, independent site. Reuses the existing THAI RESTAURANT type (Phanthong Thai, Ancoats). Closes a real gap: Didsbury has no Neighbourhood-favourite-register Eat venue distinct from its existing fine-dining/small-plates/gastropub lineup (Lime Tree, Volta, FOLK). Moderate-high confidence — well-reviewed, current, no closure signals, only caveat is the borderline district-boundary geocode noted above.

suggestions.name: Chapters
suggestions.reason: A bookshop with a wine list on Watergate Row, run by two childhood best friends who'd rather host a book club than a happy hour — browse first, then stay for the glass.
suggestions.researchNotes: Re-tallied Manchester/Cheshire tile coverage against the current venues.json + pending/approved suggestions before researching (script-assisted count, CATEGORY_BY_VENUE_TYPE mapping applied): Chester's real Drink category is genuinely thin — Huxley's (WINE BAR) is the only mapped Drink venue; Beer Heroes and Craft & Company exist but their BOTTLE SHOP/GIN BAR types aren't wired into CATEGORY_BY_VENUE_TYPE, and the pending Barlounge candidate is the only other Drink-mapped entry in the queue. Verified via chester.nub.news ('Chapters: Chester's new bookshop and wine bar opens this weekend', 'Chester's newest independent bookshop and wine bar to open this month'), chesterstandard.co.uk and Yahoo News UK: Chapters, 13 Watergate Street Row, Chester CH1 2LE, opened 21 March 2026 — an independent bookshop and wine bar owned by childhood friends Megan Nicolaides and Megan Yapp (backgrounds in accountancy and marketing, not hospitality groups), hosting book clubs, author talks and wine tastings alongside browsable fiction/non-fiction stock. No second site or group ownership found anywhere in searches; single-site, passes Hard rule 1 cleanly. Considered and rejected a nearby alternative, Café Barbette (Exchange Square) — verified as owned by QVO Hospitality, the group behind Maray, which runs multiple sites across both Liverpool and Manchester; a genuine multi-city footprint, dropped per Hard rule 1's 'when genuinely unsure, drop' guidance rather than risk it. Coordinates (53.1903/-2.8912) triangulated between Chester's own Eastgate Clock landmark (53.1909/-2.8888, already in districts.json) and the already-catalogued Barlounge (75 Watergate Street, 53.1895/-2.8947) — Chapters' low street number (13) sits close to The Cross, so weighted toward the Eastgate end; doogal.co.uk/api.postcodes.io both blocked this session, flagged for the reviewer to tighten. Typed WINE BAR (the more operationally distinctive register versus BOOKSHOP, and the one that closes the real Drink gap) rather than introducing a new hybrid type. High confidence — well-documented recent opening, independently owned, no closure signals.

suggestions.name: RAW Studios
suggestions.reason: Manchester's first pilates-sauna-ice-bath room, on Radium Street — Katie and Tom built the contrast-therapy circuit the city didn't have yet, not a gym bolting a cold plunge on as an afterthought.
suggestions.researchNotes: Ancoats' real Do category (Hallé St Peter's, Hope Mill Theatre, The Horsfall, Social Refuge, plus the pending Rubber Ducky Records candidate) had no spa/wellness-tile venue before this addition, and Ancoats sits at only 13 real venues, among the thinner Manchester districts. Verified via themanc.com/Facebook opening coverage and the venue's own site (rawstudios.uk): RAW Studios, 35 Radium Street, Manchester M4 6AD, Ancoats — described as Manchester's first studio combining Pilates (mat and reformer), barre and contrast therapy (sauna and ice bath), co-founded by Katie and Tom. No second site, franchise structure or group ownership found anywhere in searches (checked specifically given how many Manchester pilates studios turned out to be franchises this run — RE:SCULPT, on Great Ancoats Street, was researched and rejected for exactly this: a franchise model with London and multiple Manchester sites); RAW Studios reads as genuinely independent and single-site, passes Hard rule 1 cleanly. Coordinates (53.4838/-2.2255) approximated for Radium Street, near Ancoats' New Islington-facing cluster — doogal.co.uk/api.postcodes.io both blocked this session, flagged for the reviewer to tighten. Reuses the existing WELLNESS STUDIO type (Wilmslow Pilates & Wellness). Moderate-high confidence — recently opened so less review history than an established venue, but well-documented via multiple independent sources and its own site, no closure signal (nothing yet to close).

suggestions.name: Artzu Gallery
suggestions.reason: Nick Betney's own gallery since 1998, now inside the old Granada TV studios on Quay Street — Manchester's most progressive independent, still picking the artists itself rather than renting the walls out.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via theskinny.co.uk, artrabbit.com and visitmanchester.com: Artzu Gallery, Old Granada Studios, Quay Street, Manchester M60 9EA — founded by Nick Betney in 1998, described as 'Manchester's most progressive independent art gallery'; the gallery was briefly based in Spinningfields itself before settling at its current Quay Street/Old Granada Studios address. No second site or group ownership found anywhere in searches; single-site, single-owner, passes Hard rule 1 cleanly. Coordinates (53.478879/-2.255808) are a real, independently verified landmark geocode for Old Granada Studios itself (found via web search, not a postcode approximation). District placement: this point sits roughly 0.3km from the Spinningfields district centroid (53.4794/-2.2516) versus roughly 0.55km from Deansgate's (53.4762/-2.2487) — placed in Spinningfields as the closer, better-fitting district by real distance, not by category need alone, though it also happens to close a real gap (Spinningfields' Do category — Club de Padel, King Street Townhouse Spa, The Pollen Club — had no art gallery before this addition). Reuses the existing ART GALLERY type. High confidence — 25+ years of continuous trading under the same owner, well-documented, no closure signals.

suggestions.name: Church Street Gallery
